target.title: fix(state): replace non-null assertion with explicit guard for nextSessionId
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a non-null assertion (`!`) on `params.nextSessionId` could silently produce an undefined session ID if the upstream `Boolean()` guards are refactored away. TypeScript would not catch this drift.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace `params.nextSessionId!` with an explicit early return guard that TypeScript can track via control flow narrowing. The `Boolean(params.nextSessionId)` guard in the `shouldRewriteSession` condition does not narrow the parameter type for TS, so the `!` assertion was the only thing preventing `undefined` from flowing into `run.sessionId`. An explicit `if (!params.nextSessionId) return;` makes the contract visible and compiler-checked.

## User Impact

None. This is a defensive hardening that preserves existing behavior on all paths.

## Evidence

- **Real environment tested**: Linux, Node 22, `fix/remove-nextSessionId-bang-assertion`
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  
  ```
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/queue/state.test.ts
  ```
  
- **Evidence after fix**:
  
  ```console
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
       Tests  4 passed (4)
  ```
  
- **Observed result after fix**: All tests pass. Behavior unchanged on all existing paths.
- **What was not tested**: No test exercises the new early return path (which only fires when `nextSessionId` is unexpectedly missing — a precondition violation).

## Regression Test Plan

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/queue/state.test.ts
```

---
